questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on his glans penis for 3 weeks. The ulcer has a clean base, indurated edges and is non-tender on palpation. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged but non-tender. Which test is most appropriate to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.exp: The description is classic for primary syphilis (chancre). Dark-field microscopy of serous exudate directly visualises Treponema pallidum spirochetes and is the gold standard for diagnosing primary syphilis when the ulcer is active.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with butterfly-shaped erythema on the face, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers is found to have ANA positive at 1:640. Which antibody, if positive, is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibody has the highest specificity (~99%) for SLE though sensitivity is low (~25%). Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus; anti-Ro is seen in neonatal lupus and Sjogren's syndrome.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male develops rapidly spreading necrotic skin with crepitus on his thigh. Blood cultures grow Clostridium perfringens. What is the most important immediate management?
questions.exp: Necrotising fasciitis requires urgent aggressive surgical debridement of all necrotic tissue combined with broad-spectrum IV antibiotics. Delay in surgery significantly increases mortality. Hyperbaric oxygen is adjunctive, not primary therapy.

questions.q: A 22-year-old student has well-defined hypopigmented macules on the chest with fine branny scaling. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatball' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur. The KOH mount showing short hyphae and round spores gives the 'spaghetti and meatball' appearance. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow or coppery-orange fluorescence.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lip, fever and cervical lymphadenopathy. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. This is the child's first episode. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary HSV-1 infection typically manifests as herpetic gingivostomatitis in children with high fever, painful vesicles/ulcers on gingiva and oral mucosa, drooling, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Tzanck cells (multinucleated giant cells) confirm herpetic infection.

questions.q: A 30-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops acute painful nodular lesions on the face and trunk with fever, malaise and neuritis. Skin biopsy shows neutrophilic infiltration with foamy macrophages containing fragmented bacilli. What type of reaction is this?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction (immune complex-mediated, Type III hypersensitivity) occurring in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy. It is characterised by painful erythematous nodules, systemic features, and neutrophilic infiltration on biopsy. Treatment is thalidomide or systemic steroids.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman has tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin. Histopathology shows subepidermal blister with eosinophilic infiltrate. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense (subepidermal) bullae, eosinophilic infiltrate, and linear IgG + C3 at the BMZ on DIF. The autoantigens are BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230. Pemphigus shows intraepidermal blisters with intercellular IgG; DH shows granular IgA at papillary dermis tips.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male with erythematous plaques and silvery-white scales over the scalp, elbows and knees now reports DIP joint pain. Nail examination shows pitting, onycholysis and oil-drop sign. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis characteristically involves DIP joints (unlike RA which spares DIP). Nail involvement - pitting, onycholysis, oil-drop/salmon-patch sign - is strongly associated with psoriatic arthritis and present in up to 80% of cases.

questions.q: A 25-year-old atopic individual has intensely pruritic lichenified plaques in the antecubital and popliteal fossae, elevated serum IgE, and a personal history of childhood asthma. Which cytokines are primarily responsible for the Th2-driven inflammation?
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis is primarily Th2-mediated. IL-4 drives IgE class switching and Th2 differentiation; IL-13 perpetuates allergic inflammation and contributes to barrier dysfunction. Dupilumab targets the shared IL-4Ralpha receptor of both IL-4 and IL-13.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman has progressive skin tightening over the face and fingers with Raynaud's phenomenon, difficulty opening her mouth, and dysphagia. Which antibody is most specifically associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc and carries high risk of pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST syndrome). Anti-RNA pol III is associated with scleroderma renal crisis.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male has multiple painless ulcers on the scrotum. Culture on chocolate agar requires factors X and V and shows satellite phenomenon around Staphylococcus aureus colonies. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Haemophilus ducreyi causes chancroid - painful genital ulcers with soft, undermined, ragged edges. It requires factors X (hemin) and V (NAD) and shows satellite phenomenon on blood agar around Staphylococcus aureus. The ulcers in chancroid are painful (unlike syphilitic chancre).

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer has a pearly, translucent papule with rolled borders and telangiectasias on his nose for 2 years. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels. What is the most likely diagnosis and cell of origin?
opts: Basal cell carcinoma - pluripotent cells of the basal layer
questions.exp: Nodular BCC presents as a pearly, translucent papule with rolled borders and telangiectasias on sun-exposed areas (nose most common). Arborizing (tree-like) vessels on dermoscopy are pathognomonic. BCC arises from pluripotent cells of the basal layer of epidermis or hair follicle.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman has a warty hyperkeratotic plaque on the lower leg for 20 years. Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with atypical keratinocytes and no dermal invasion. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bowen's disease is SCC in situ characterised by full-thickness epidermal dysplasia without dermal invasion. Actinic keratosis shows only partial-thickness dysplasia. Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing, self-resolving lesion with a keratin-filled central crater.

questions.q: A woman with lupus erythematosus delivers a baby with complete heart block and cutaneous annular erythema. Which maternal antibody crosses the placenta to cause this neonatal syndrome?
questions.exp: Neonatal lupus is caused by transplacental passage of maternal anti-Ro/SSA (and anti-La/SSB) antibodies. The most serious manifestation is congenital complete heart block due to fibrosis of the conduction system. Mothers may have SLE or primary Sjogren's syndrome.

questions.q: A 15-year-old presents with intensely pruritic papules and burrows in the web spaces of fingers and wrists. His roommate has similar complaints. Dermoscopy reveals a delta-wing jet shape at the end of a burrow. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: 5% permethrin cream applied from neck downward left overnight (8-10 hours) and repeated after 1 week is the topical first-line treatment for scabies. The delta-wing jet sign (Concorde sign) on dermoscopy represents the mite. All household contacts must be treated simultaneously.

questions.q: A 42-year-old presents with a non-healing ulcer on the dorsum of the foot for 6 months. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with granulomas and broad, non-septate hyphae branching at right angles in tissue. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Entomophthoromycosis (subcutaneous zygomycosis caused by Basidiobolus or Conidiobolus) shows broad non-septate hyphae branching at 90 degrees (characteristic of Zygomycetes). Chromoblastomycosis shows muriform/sclerotic bodies. Mycetoma has grains. Sporotrichosis shows cigar-shaped yeast.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive man has multiple painless, flesh-coloured, umbilicated papules over the face and trunk. Electron microscopy of the lesion shows 'brick-shaped' viral particles. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by a poxvirus (brick-shaped EM particles with a dumbbell-shaped DNA core). In HIV, MC can be giant and numerous. Pathognomonic histological feature: Henderson-Paterson bodies (large eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions).

questions.q: A 28-year-old has an asymmetric hypopigmented anaesthetic patch on the forearm with loss of all modalities of sensation. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows epithelioid cell granulomas with lymphocytic infiltrate and nerve destruction. What is the Ridley-Jopling classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) has 1-2 well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, complete loss of all sensation modalities, negative slit-skin smear, and well-formed epithelioid granulomas destroying the nerve on biopsy. BT would have 2-5 lesions; LL shows positive SSS and diffuse skin infiltration.

questions.q: A patient develops target lesions and mucosal erosions of mouth, eyes and genitalia following trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Nikolsky sign is negative. The rash covers less than 10% BSA with mucosal involvement at 2 sites. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) is defined by mucosal erosions at 2 or more sites plus atypical target lesions covering less than 10% BSA. TEN involves more than 30% BSA epidermal detachment. Sulfonamides are among the most common triggers of SJS.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman on long-term chloroquine for rheumatoid arthritis is referred for routine ophthalmologic screening. Which macular pattern is pathognomonic of chloroquine retinopathy?
questions.exp: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can cause irreversible bull's-eye maculopathy - a ring of depigmentation surrounding a central island of preserved foveal pigment. This toxicity is dose-dependent and cumulative. Annual ophthalmologic screening after 5 years of use is recommended.

questions.q: A 19-year-old male is started on oral isotretinoin 1 mg/kg/day for severe nodulocystic acne. Which of the following is the most critical counselling point for his female partner of childbearing age?
opts: Use two forms of contraception - drug is highly teratogenic
questions.exp: Isotretinoin is one of the most potent teratogens (Category X). It causes craniofacial, cardiac, CNS, and thymic defects. Female patients of childbearing potential must use two effective contraceptive methods starting 1 month before, during, and 1 month after treatment. Monthly pregnancy tests are mandatory.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a facial BCC. What is the primary advantage of this technique over conventional wide local excision?
opts: Provides 100% margin assessment with maximum tissue conservation
Can be performed without pathological examination
questions.exp: Mohs surgery involves sequential horizontal tissue sectioning with immediate frozen-section examination of 100% of peripheral and deep margins (vs ~1% in conventional bread-loaf sectioning). This allows complete margin control while maximising conservation of healthy tissue - crucial for cosmetically sensitive facial sites.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with palpable purpura on bilateral lower limbs, haematuria, and arthralgias following an URTI. Renal biopsy shows IgA deposits in the mesangium. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (HSP) is a small vessel vasculitis characterised by palpable purpura (non-thrombocytopenic), arthralgia, abdominal pain, and IgA nephropathy. Mesangial IgA deposits on renal biopsy and IgA deposits on skin biopsy confirm the diagnosis. It commonly follows a viral URTI.

questions.q: A 29-year-old woman from Turkey has recurrent painful oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis. Pathergy test is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease is a multi-system vasculitis characterised by recurrent oral ulcers (sine qua non), genital ulcers, ocular involvement (uveitis, hypopyon), and skin lesions. Pathergy test (non-specific skin hyperreactivity to needlestick) is positive. Prevalence peaks along the ancient Silk Road (Turkey, Iran, Japan).

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman presents with 3-month history of generalised pruritus without primary skin lesions, weight loss and night sweats. Which underlying malignancy is most classically associated with generalised pruritus as a paraneoplastic manifestation?
questions.exp: Generalised pruritus sine materia is a classic paraneoplastic manifestation of Hodgkin lymphoma, occurring in up to 25% of patients and potentially preceding diagnosis by months. The mechanism involves pruritogenic cytokines (IL-31, histamine) from Reed-Sternberg cells. Pruritus resolves with lymphoma treatment.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with proximal muscle weakness and violaceous discolouration of the eyelids with periorbital oedema. He has flat-topped violaceous papules over the dorsal MCP and PIP joints. What is the eponymous name for these papules?
questions.exp: Gottron's papules are pathognomonic of dermatomyositis - flat-topped violaceous papules over the dorsal MCP and PIP joints (not DIP). Heliotrope rash (violaceous periorbital erythema with oedema) is also characteristic. Gottron's sign refers to macular erythema at the same sites without papules.

questions.q: A 33-year-old woman has firm skin-coloured papules in the nasolabial folds, subungual fibromas, and a shagreen patch on the lower back since childhood. Her mother has similar features. What is the inheritance pattern?
questions.exp: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is autosomal dominant, caused by mutations in TSC1 (hamartin) or TSC2 (tuberin). Cutaneous features include angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum) in nasolabial folds, periungual fibromas (Koenen tumours), shagreen patches, ash-leaf macules, and cafe-au-lait spots.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman has thickening, discolouration, and crumbling of all toenails with subungual hyperkeratosis and onycholysis. KOH mount of nail scrapings shows septate hyphae. Which organism is the most common cause of this condition?
questions.exp: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common cause of onychomycosis worldwide, accounting for ~70-80% of cases, predominantly causing distal-lateral subungual onychomycosis (DLSO). Oral terbinafine is the drug of choice. Candida causes onychomycosis mainly in immunocompromised patients.

questions.q: A dermatologist performs a punch biopsy for a suspected melanocytic lesion. At what angle should the punch be held relative to the skin surface for optimal tissue sampling?
opts: 30 degrees angle following relaxed skin tension lines
90 degrees perpendicular to the skin surface
60 degrees angle away from critical structures
questions.exp: A punch biopsy should be held perpendicular (90 degrees) to the skin surface to ensure a cylindrical core including epidermis, dermis, and upper subcutaneous fat. The punch is rotated in one direction with downward pressure until a loss of resistance is felt indicating subcutaneous entry.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman on oral contraceptive pills develops brownish macules on sun-exposed areas of her face that worsen in summer and fade slightly in winter. Wood's lamp accentuates the pigmentation. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Melasma is acquired hypermelanosis on sun-exposed areas (cheeks, forehead, upper lip - centrofacial pattern most common), exacerbated by UV radiation, pregnancy, and OCPs. Wood's lamp accentuates epidermal-type melasma. Treatment: broad-spectrum sunscreen plus triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + corticosteroid).

questions.q: A 45-year-old male with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis on methotrexate 15 mg weekly for 6 months develops abnormal liver function tests. After what cumulative dose of methotrexate is liver biopsy (or non-invasive equivalent) traditionally recommended?
questions.exp: Liver biopsy was traditionally recommended after every 1-1.5 g cumulative dose of methotrexate. Non-invasive methods (Fibroscan/transient elastography, procollagen-III-N-terminal peptide - P3NP) are now preferred. Folic acid supplementation reduces mucosal and haematological toxicity without affecting anti-psoriatic efficacy.
